title: Evaluations detect equivalences in localized strict model diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal M$ be an ordinary category with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits, equipped with classes $C,F,W$. Assume that $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. Here a weak factorization system consists of a factorization of every arrow into the two classes, each class being characterized by diagonal lifting against the other. Let $0$ be initial and let $\mathcal M_c$ be the full subcategory on objects $X$ with $0\to X\in C$. For a $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $I$, let $W_I$ consist of natural transformations in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c)$ whose components lie in $W$. In sufficiently large universes put
$$\mathcal B=N(\mathcal M_c)[W^{-1}]_\infty,\qquad \mathcal A_I=N(\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c))[W_I^{-1}]_\infty.$$
Each localization is characterized by restriction giving, into every quasicategory, an equivalence on the entire functor quasicategory with the full subcategory of functors inverting the indicated arrows. Evaluation followed by localization induces $\operatorname{ev}_i^L:\mathcal A_I\to\mathcal B$ for $i\in I$. For every arrow $a$ of $\mathcal A_I$, if $\operatorname{ev}_i^L(a)$ is an equivalence for every $i\in I$, then $a$ is an equivalence. Equivalently, the induced evaluation comparison $\mathcal A_I\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal B)$ is conservative, meaning that it reflects equivalences. No model structure on $\mathcal M^I$, simplicial enrichment, combinatoriality or properness is assumed. The empty category $I$ is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 7.9.8, printed p. 410, conservativity paragraph between (7.9.8.6) and (7.9.8.7), for the nerve of the cofibrant part of an ordinary model category; the model-category saturation and the cofibration-category fraction calculus supply its hypotheses. Remark 7.9.7 checks heredity by sequential lifting. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c)$. Let $U$ consist of componentwise trivial cofibrations and $V$ of componentwise trivial fibrations in $D$. Identities belong to both lifting classes of a weak factorization system, hence to $W$; two-out-of-three gives composition closure of $W$. The lifting-class closure of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] makes $C$ and $C\cap W$ closed under composition and pushout. The dual pullback and composition assertions for right lifting classes follow directly: a square against a pullback projects to a square against the original right-class map, whose lift pairs with the given base map to give a lift into the pullback; successive right-class maps are handled by two successive lifts. Thus $F\cap W$ is closed under pullback and composition. In particular composition makes $U,V$ subcategories. Choose the stated functorial factorization of $0\to X$ to obtain $QX\to X$ in $F\cap W$ with $QX$ cofibrant. All these constructions applied pointwise are functors on strict $I$-diagrams: their structural maps are the images of commuting squares under the functorial choices. Pointwise pullbacks and pushouts exist in $\mathcal M$ because the shapes are finite. This does not assert a model structure on $D$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: elementary lifting consequences and pointwise replacements beneath the strict diagram fraction argument

proof.text: For a map $w:A\to B$ in $W_I$, factor it pointwise and functorially as $A\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}B$ with $u\in C$ and $v\in F\cap W$. The objects $E(i)$ are cofibrant by composition, and two-out-of-three gives $u\in U$, while $v\in V$. A span $X'\xleftarrow{u}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $u\in U$ has the pointwise pushout $Y'=X'\amalg_XY$: the map $Y\to Y'$ is in $U$ and $Y'$ is objectwise cofibrant. A cospan $X\xrightarrow{g}Y\xleftarrow{v}Y'$ with $v\in V$ has pointwise pullback $P=X\times_Y Y'$. Replace $P$ functorially by $QP\to P$. Then $QP\to X$ is a composite of trivial fibrations, hence in $V$, and $QP$ is objectwise cofibrant. These are commuting squares in $D$; they exist without properness. The replacement is necessary because the raw pullback need not be cofibrant.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: explicit factorization and square completions for strict cofibrant diagrams

proof.text: Write $Q_D:D\to D[W_I^{-1}]$ for ordinary localization, constructed by finite words in arrows and formal inverses to $W_I$, modulo composition and inverse relations. Every generator $f:X\to Y$ is the three-arrow word $X\xleftarrow{1}X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xleftarrow{1}Y$; the inverse of $w:Y\to X$ is $X\xleftarrow{w}Y\xrightarrow{1}Y\xleftarrow{1}Y$. To compose $X\xleftarrow{a}A\xrightarrow{f}B\xleftarrow{b}Y$ and $Y\xleftarrow{c}C\xrightarrow{g}E\xleftarrow{d}Z$, factor $bc:C\to B$ as $C\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{v}B$ with $u\in U,v\in V$. Use step 2 to complete $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xleftarrow{v}T$ to $P\xrightarrow{t}T$, $P\xrightarrow{p}A$ with $p\in V$ and $vt=fp$. Push out $u:C\to T$ against $g:C\to E$, obtaining $k:T\to H$ and $j:E\to H$ with $j\in U$ and $ku=jg$. The composite is represented by $X\xleftarrow{ap}P\xrightarrow{kt}H\xleftarrow{jd}Z$. Indeed $Q_D(kt)Q_D(p)^{-1}=Q_D(j)Q_D(g)Q_D(bc)^{-1}Q_D(f)$, by the two displayed commuting-square equations. The outer maps $ap,jd$ lie in $W_I$. Induction on the number of generators, with the identity as the empty word, now represents every localized morphism by such a three-arrow word. Only formal inverse algebra is used after the constructions of step 2.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: complete finite-word induction supplying the fraction reduction

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] to $(D,W_I)$. It identifies $h\mathcal A_I$ with $D[W_I^{-1}]$, naturally for evaluations. By its essential-surjectivity clause, conjugate any given arrow $a$ by equivalences at its endpoints so that those endpoints are images of strict diagrams. This conjugation preserves both the assumption on the evaluations and the desired conclusion. Steps 2-3 then represent $[a]$ by $Q_D(b)^{-1}Q_D(f)Q_D(a_0)^{-1}$, with $a_0:A\to X$, $f:A\to B$, $b:Y\to B$, and $a_0,b\in W_I$. The homotopy-category comparison ensures this assertion concerns the given arrow, not merely objects of a localization.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: passage to the ordinary homotopy category and representation of the actual arrow

proof.text: Let $\gamma:\mathcal M\to H=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ be ordinary localization, constructed by finite words in a larger universe. The nerve of $\gamma|_{\mathcal M_c}$ inverts $W$, so the stated full coherent universal property of $\mathcal B$ gives $T:\mathcal B\to N(H)$ with an equivalence after restriction to $N(\mathcal M_c)$. Suppose all $\operatorname{ev}_i^L(a)$ are equivalences. Applying $T$ and homotopy categories to the fraction of step 4, its outer factors become isomorphisms since $a_{0,i},b_i\in W$. Thus $\gamma(f_i)$ is an isomorphism for each $i$. Naturality of the comparison in [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] identifies this calculation with evaluation of the original class $[a]$, up to the endpoint conjugations already allowed. The next three steps show $f_i\in W$ from the two smaller ordinary homotopy lemmas, without citing the cyclic general saturation node.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: apply the ordinary localization to each component of the strict fraction

proof.text: Fix $i$ and write $u=f_i:A\to B$; both $A,B$ are cofibrant. Functorially factor $X\to *$ as $X\xrightarrow{r_X}RX\to *$, with $r_X\in C\cap W$ and $RX$ fibrant. Then $RA,RB$ are also cofibrant by composition. Naturality gives $Ru\,r_A=r_Bu$, so $\gamma(Ru)$ is an isomorphism because $\gamma(u),\gamma(r_A),\gamma(r_B)$ are. Factor $Ru$ as $RA\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}RB$, with $j\in C\cap W$ and $p\in F$. Then $E$ is cofibrant (composition with $0\to RA$) and fibrant (composition with $RB\to *$). The map $\gamma(p)$ is invertible. By [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective], applied with cofibrant source $RB$ and fibrant target $E$, choose $s:RB\to E$ with $\gamma(s)=\gamma(p)^{-1}$. Hence $\gamma(ps)=1$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: bifibrant replacement of the fixed component and representation of one inverse

proof.text: For each cofibrant $X$, factor its fold map $X\amalg X\to X$ as a cofibration $(e_0,e_1):X\amalg X\to J_X$ followed by a trivial fibration $c_X:J_X\to X$. This is a good cylinder: $c_Xe_k=1$ and $c_X\in W$. Each coproduct injection $X\to X\amalg X$ is a cofibration, since its missing summand lifts against any trivial fibration by cofibrancy of $X$; hence each $e_k$ is a cofibration, and two-out-of-three makes it trivial. A good path object for every fibrant $Y$ is obtained by factoring its diagonal $Y\to Y\times Y$ into a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration. These choices meet every hypothesis of [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test]. Apply its equality-to-cylinder clause to $ps,1_{RB}:RB\to RB$. It gives $H:J_{RB}\to RB$ with $He_0=ps$ and $He_1=1$. Lift the square with top $s:RB\to E$, left $e_0$, right $p$, and bottom $H$. This yields $V:J_{RB}\to E$ with $Ve_0=s$ and $pV=H$. Set $t=Ve_1$; then $pt=1_{RB}$, and since $\gamma(p)$ is invertible, $\gamma(tp)=1_{\gamma E}$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: specified good cylinder and lifting square rectify the component inverse to a strict section

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] again, now to $tp,1_E:E\to E$, with the good cylinder $E\xrightarrow{d_0,d_1}J_E\xrightarrow{c_E}E$ just constructed and any good path object for $E$. It gives $G:J_E\to E$ with $Gd_0=tp$ and $Gd_1=1_E$. The equations $c_Ed_k=1_E$, with $c_E\in W$, give $d_0,d_1\in W$. Then $Gd_1=1_E$ gives $G\in W$, whence $tp=Gd_0\in W$. In the arrow category, $p:E\to RB$ is a retract of $tp:E\to E$: the arrow maps are $(1_E,t)$ and $(1_E,p)$, their squares commute since $pt=1$, and their composite on $p$ is $(1_E,pt)=1_p$. Retract closure gives $p\in W$. Therefore $Ru=pj\in W$, and $Ru\,r_A=r_Bu$ gives $u\in W$ by two-out-of-three. This proves $f_i\in W$ for every $i$ by an explicit homotopy and retract calculation; it assumes neither a model structure on the diagram category nor rectification.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: second cylinder and explicit arrow retract recover the weak-equivalence condition on each component

proof.text: Consequently $f\in W_I$. In the fraction of step 4 all three arrows now belong to $W_I$, so $[a]$ is invertible in $h\mathcal A_I$. The equivalence-edge criterion of [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] implies that the original arrow $a$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal A_I$, including the endpoint conjugations. This finishes detection for arbitrary arrows of the coherent localization, not only those originally in the diagram category.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: invert the three fraction factors and return to the given coherent arrow

proof.text: The induced comparison has $i$th component $\operatorname{ev}_i^L$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], its image of an arrow is an equivalence exactly when all these components are equivalences, so the just-proved detection assertion is exactly conservativity. When $I$ is empty, $D$ is the terminal ordinary category and $W_I$ is its single identity. The homotopy-category comparison of [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] makes $h\mathcal A_I$ equivalent to the terminal category, so every arrow of $\mathcal A_I$ is an equivalence. This verifies the vacuous evaluation hypothesis without requiring an object of $I$.
